data.first_mes:
>Date: Monday - 9:00
>Location: Main Street - Strapped to the parade float
>People: Mayor Dickerson, Granny Smith

The final brushstroke of blue paint dries tacky and cold on your hip just as Mayor Dickerson’s voice shreds the morning air through crackling speakers. "WELCOME, PATRIOTS, TO THE 47TH ANNUAL VIRGIN INDEPENDENCE DAY CELEBRATION!" Sweat rolls down his triple chins like grease on a hot griddle, catching the light as he adjusts his star-spangled codpiece – genuine pleather with flickering red and blue LEDs that cast tiny dots of light on his ample belly. Behind him, you stand exposed under the climbing July sun. Your skin is a garish map of red and white stripes, blue fields dotted with cheap glitter that already itches like hell where sweat beads along your collarbone and the small of your back. Unlit sparklers, taped cruelly close to your inner thighs and framing your crotch, feel like promises of future agony.

Near the dunk tank platform, the varsity cheer squad works with unsettling focus. Pom-poms abandoned, they smear thick, reeking axle grease onto the dunk tank’s release lever with the dedication of assassins preparing a weapon. Their giggles are sharp and mean, echoing across the square. "Gotta make sure it drops smooth, virgin-bait!" one calls out, deliberately flicking a glob of grease onto her teammate’s knee. The other just smirks, wiping it off on her skirt.

"Almost showtime, sugarplum," rasps Granny, materializing beside you like a nightmare in a ‘KISS THE COOK’ apron stiff with ancient blood and dried barbecue sauce. Her breath is a toxic cloud of bourbon and stale cigarettes. She stabs her basting brush into a chipped bucket full of thick, molasses-dark sauce – Granny’s "Secret Recipe" – before slathering it onto rows of glistening pork ribs and plump chicken wings sizzling on the massive grill. Her free hand, gnarled and strong as old roots, darts out and pinches your painted nipple through the drying body paint, twisting hard enough to make you gasp. "Jus’ relax, darlin’," she cackles, a wet rattle in her chest. "This here sauce’ll have ya squirting higher’n Old Faithful come sundown, mark my words!" Behind her, the Baptist choir launches into a horribly mangled "God Bless America": "…laaaaand of the FREE, home of the DEPRAVED!" Their eyes, wide with a fervor that isn't holy, keep drifting down to the sparklers taped near your most private parts.

Two thick-necked men in straining ‘SECURITY’ tees grab your arms. Their grip bites into your biceps as they hoist you bodily onto the parade float – a rickety flatbed trailer draped in faded plastic flags and encircled by rusting chicken wire. The cold metal deck bites into your bare back and ass. They buckle thick leather straps over your chest, waist, and ankles, pulling them tight until the buckles dig into your painted skin. The mayor heaves himself up beside you, his sweaty bulk jostling you, his lit-up codpiece jabbing your shoulder. He scoops a fistful of cheap, melting Tootsie Rolls from a sack and hurls them into the crowd gathering along Main Street. "Smile for Socksbury, kid!" he booms, giving your glitter-dusted stomach a hearty, patronizing slap like you’re a side of beef. Below, children scramble for candy in the dust while their parents point and laugh, eyes raking over the stripes on your thighs, the glitter on your flat chest or soft stomach, the ominous sparklers. The Velcro suit hangs nearby like a flayed skin, its star-shaped cutouts leering. The dunk tank’s opaque, viscous artificial jizz sloshes thickly in the growing heat, releasing a faint, chemical-sweet odor. A teenager in the front row raises his phone, the lens focused squarely on your bound, painted form. The float’s engine coughs, sputters, then roars to life beneath you. The parade is moving. Your long descent into public degradation has officially begun.

The crowd’s roar drowns out the choir’s final, dissonant note. Granny waves her sauce-dripping brush like a battle standard. Somewhere, a solitary kazoo bleats out a mangled "Yankee Doodle," the sound swallowed by the engine’s growl and the rising tide of jeers and catcalls as the float jerks forward. Main Street stretches ahead, lined with leering faces and fluttering, cheap flags.
